answer_text:
# 🦴 Calcium-Containing Foods

Calcium is a mineral used for numerous functions, including building bones and teeth, muscle contraction, blood clotting, maintenance of cell membranes, and nerve transmission. It is the most abundant mineral in your body and a major component of your bones and teeth — but your body can't make calcium on its own, so it's essential to consume calcium-rich foods to meet your daily needs.

---

## 🥛 Dairy Products (Highest Sources)

Dairy products (milk, cheese, yogurt, etc.) are the most concentrated food sources of calcium — for example, one cup of milk contains approximately 271 mg of calcium.

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|----------------|
| **Parmesan Cheese** | 242 mg per oz (24% DV) |
| **Yogurt (plain, whole milk)** | ~206 mg per 6 oz |
| **Milk** | ~271 mg per cup |
| **Swiss Cheese** | Very high (one of the richest sources) |

Yogurt is an excellent source of calcium, and many types are also rich in probiotics — a type of beneficial bacteria that can promote immune function, improve heart health, and enhance nutrient absorption.

Most cheeses are excellent sources of calcium. Parmesan cheese has the most, with 242 mg — or 24% of the Daily Value — per ounce (28 grams). Softer cheeses tend to have less.

---

## 🐟 Seafood

Sardines and canned salmon are loaded with calcium, thanks to their edible bones. Canned pink salmon provides about **241 mg per 3 oz** serving.

---

## 🌿 Plant-Based Sources

Tofu is the most concentrated source of non-dairy calcium.

Seeds are tiny nutritional powerhouses, and many are high in calcium, including poppy, sesame, celery, and chia seeds.

Many plant foods are also calcium-rich, including greens, beans, tofu, nuts, and seeds.

| Plant-Based Food | Notes |
|-----------------|-------|
| **Tofu** | Top non-dairy source |
| **Kale & Bok Choy** | Good absorption |
| **Broccoli** | Good bioavailability |
| **White/Black Beans** | ~239 mg per cup (raw) |
| **Chia & Sesame Seeds** | Excellent per tablespoon |
| **Almonds** | Good source of calcium |
| **Rhubarb** | ~105 mg per cup (raw) |
| **Turnip Greens** | ~209 mg per cup (cooked) |

---

## 🥣 Fortified Foods

Fortified foods like cereals can make it easier to meet your daily calcium needs. You can also find a variety of plant-based beverages, such as plant milks and orange juice, that have been fortified with calcium.

---

## ⚠️ Important Tips

- The absorption of calcium from dairy products and fortified foods is about 30%. Certain compounds in plants (e.g., oxalic acid, phytic acid) can decrease calcium absorption by forming indigestible salts with calcium.

- The bioavailability of calcium from plants that do not contain these compounds — including broccoli, kale, and cabbage — is similar to that of milk, although the amount of calcium per serving is much lower.

- Vitamin D is crucial for increasing calcium absorption in the body. If you're not getting regular sun exposure, try consuming foods rich in vitamin D, like milk.

- Recommended Dietary Allowances for calcium range from **1,000 to 1,200 mg for adults** and from 200 to 1,300 mg for infants, children, and adolescents, depending on age.

Eating a **variety of calcium-rich foods** from both dairy and plant sources throughout the day is the best way to meet your daily calcium needs! 💪
